source_title: Is Neil McCann's Kilmarnock style 'unsustainable'? - BBC
source_excerpt:
Former Kilmarnock goalkeeper Cammy Bell believes boss Neil McCann's expansive style is "unsustainable".
McCann saved the club from relegation last term but they have failed to kick on in the new campaign.
Kilmarnock currently sit bottom of the Premiership with only two wins out of their opening 11 league fixtures and 26 goals conceded.
Not only that, they have faced the most shots, shots on target, given away the most big chances and scored the joint fewest goals.
As pressure builds on McCann among the Kilmarnock support, Cammy Bell told the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast what he thinks is going wrong for his former club.
"They need to stop conceding goals. You look at the amount of goals that they've conceded already this season and that has been a theme since McCann came in," said Bell.
"He's quite expansive in the style he wants to play. They've conceded 26 goals, that is just unsustainable to win games.
"You will not win games if you concede that many goals. They've only scored 11, so that tells you Kilmarnock why they are bottom. It's not good enough at the moment.
"McCann needs to turn things around quickly because the fans are now starting to question what direction Kilmarnock are going in. He needs to get some points on the board quickly."
